title: The corpus v4 recipe: trajectories held out by whole project, nothing below the threshold
request: Write the recipe for corpus v4: the 330 declarative examples of v3 plus trajectory examples, split by whole project (about one in five held out), with v3's quality gates (no benchmark contamination, no near-duplicate prompts across the split). Generate nothing until at least 50 trajectories from at least 10 projects exist; until then print how many exist. Keep generated files out of version control as for out_v3.
spec: A corpus v4 recipe mixing v3's declarative examples with trajectories, held out by whole projects, with the number of held-out projects shown against the threshold. Done when the Policy model page shows 'N of 50 trajectories' from the real count and stage 2 is marked ready only at the threshold.
plan: Define a trajectory: one opted-in project's move log or one agent run on it, with at least 3 decisions.

Write studio/corpus_v4.py: next_move examples (state, the moves or tools on offer, the last three decisions -> the move made; only allowed moves and working steps) and judge_move examples (a proposed move -> the validator's verdict, failed checks and cited rules); the split by project; v3's gates; make sft-v4 writes nothing below the threshold.
Show the real count on the Policy model page and mark stage 2 ready only at both thresholds.

Run the review; it simulated 12 standard-plan projects on the Telco sample and found the gates did not work on realistic data; fix eight findings with a realistic fixture; fix the re-check's one; commit.

decisions.decision: Mask the project's own ids (<project>, <run>) in prompts and targets, and count only distinct trajectories toward the threshold.
decisions.why: Two projects that decide the same must make the same example; otherwise twenty identical standard-plan runs look like twenty trajectories and pass the duplicate gate.

decisions.decision: A project is in validation when its own id hashes there (about one in five), so it never changes split as the workspace grows; a fallback, when none hashes there, is named in the manifest.
decisions.why: Taking the first fifth by hash rank moves projects between splits when new ones arrive, so a later build would train on an earlier build's validation.

decisions.decision: A project built on a dataset v3 holds out goes to validation, recognised by sample key, file name or column set; a project on a judgment-suite table is left out.
decisions.why: v3's validation must stay unseen, and A6.3 evaluates on the judgment suite's tables, so training on them would contaminate the benchmark.

decisions.decision: Gates run within each split after the split, and a training prompt equal or near-equal to a validation prompt is dropped.
decisions.why: Removing duplicates across all projects first made the split depend on the store's list order.
Unlike out_v3, which the repository builds from its own evidence, v4 holds a workspace's projects and the repository cannot rebuild it.

change: dclab_rnd/studio/corpus_v4.py (trajectories, masking, project_meta, held_out_projects with a recorded fallback, examples, gates, status, build) and make sft-v4; the Policy model page shows 'N of 50 distinct trajectories, from P of 10 opted-in projects' from /api/learn/policy, says when the count cannot be read, and marks stage 2 ready only at both thresholds; sft/out_v4 in .gitignore; tests/test_corpus_v4.py and tests/test_pages_learn.py.

findings.defect: The near-duplicate gate missed prompts that differ only by project id, so validation measured memory.
findings.scenario: 12 opted-in standard-plan projects on the Telco sample: step arguments carry the project id, so two projects with the same decisions have prompts identical except for the id (Jaccard 0.887, under 0.9); 50 of 50 training examples had a validation prompt identical once ids were masked, and the gate dropped only 10. A next_move target containing the id cannot be predicted from a prompt that never shows it.
findings.cause: Arguments kept the project's own ids.
findings.fix: Project and run ids are masked in prompts and targets before the gates, and only distinct masked trajectories count; the same simulation now gives 2 distinct trajectories from 1 project, not ready.

findings.defect: Projects built from Home on a dataset v3 holds out were not forced into validation.
findings.scenario: Home, the heart_disease sample, build the project, opt in: the recipe read suggestion.sample, which only the intern's use_sample sets, so the project was split by hash with an 80% chance of training on a v3 validation dataset.
findings.cause: One route to recognise a sample.
findings.fix: project_meta recognises the dataset by sample key, file name stem or column set.

findings.defect: Which examples landed in which split depended on the store's list order.
findings.scenario: The same workspace gave train 50 / val 34 as listed and train 72 / val 12 reversed; adding one project changed the validation set.
findings.cause: Exact-duplicate removal ran over all projects before the split and kept the first copy.
findings.fix: Assign by project first, remove duplicates within each split, then drop training prompts found in validation.

findings.defect: A project's split was not stable as the workspace grew.
findings.scenario: At 13 and 14 projects the first three by hash rank were held out; a new project with a lower hash pushed a former validation project into training, so a later build trained on an earlier build's validation.
findings.cause: The held-out set was the first round(n/5) projects by hash rank.
findings.fix: A per-project rule (its own hash modulo 5), as v3's split does.

findings.defect: The tests never exercised the gates or the real count.
findings.scenario: The fixture gave every project a unique state, so duplicates removed and near-duplicates were 0; switching the gate off changed nothing; one test re-applied the function under test; the page's count path was never called, and a wiring error would show '0 of 50' behind a broad except.
findings.fix: A realistic fixture with identical states and id arguments, assertions that the gates fire, the exact 50 and 10 boundary, the path-and-hash rejection, and an API test of the count and its error path.

findings.defect: The benchmark A6.3 evaluates on had no contamination gate.
findings.scenario: A workspace project built on a judgment-suite case table would put that case into training, while A6.3 measures the tuned model on those cases.
findings.cause: 'Benchmark contamination' was read as v3's validation only.
findings.fix: A project whose columns match a judgment-suite case is recognised and left out.

findings.defect: v4's gates were weaker than v3's while the row said 'the same'.
findings.scenario: The absolute-path pattern lacked /tmp/, the hash pattern matched only 64 hex characters (v3: 40 to 64), and duplicates were keyed on prompt plus answer, so identical prompts with conflicting targets stayed in one split.
findings.cause: The gates were rewritten instead of reused.
findings.fix: v3's patterns and key (the normalised user turn) are used.

findings.defect: When the count failed, the page showed '0 of 50' with no cause, and the held-out count ignored forced projects.
findings.scenario: The API returned an error field the page never rendered; the fixture's page said 2 held out while 3 were.
findings.cause: Error not rendered; the count read only hash-chosen projects.
findings.fix: The page says the count cannot be read and why; the held-out count includes forced projects.

findings.defect: The fallback held-out project could move to training as the workspace grew (re-check).
findings.scenario: At 10 projects there is about an 11% chance that none hashes to validation; the lowest-hash project is then held out, and once a project that hashes there joins, the fallback goes back to training, contradicting 'never changes split'.
findings.fix: The fallback is named in the manifest, and the docstring and status row say it can move to training later.
findings.test: The stability test checks the named fallback for three ids that do not hash to validation.

measurements.name: trajectory count against the stage-2 threshold
measurements.gate: Nothing is generated until 50 distinct trajectories from at least 10 opted-in projects exist (fixed in the package).
measurements.result: 0 of 50 distinct trajectories from 0 of 10 opted-in projects in the owner's workspace; nothing was generated. In the reviewer's simulation, 12 identical standard-plan projects gave 24 recorded but 2 distinct trajectories from 1 project: not ready.
measurements.next: A6.3 (training) waits for the threshold and the owner's approval of compute and cost.

outcome: Done: make sft-v4 and the Policy model page count distinct trajectories, hold out whole projects stably, keep v3's held-out datasets and the judgment suite out of training, and generate nothing below the threshold. Open: the threshold is not met, so no v4 file has been generated or trained on; distinctness is exact. Nine review findings fixed.
lessons: Test a dedup or split recipe on realistic duplicates (identical runs), or its gates never fire in tests.
Mask per-instance ids before comparing prompts; otherwise near-identical examples pass as different.
A held-out split must be a per-item rule, not a rank, or it moves as the data grows.
Count distinct examples toward a training threshold, or repeated runs fake readiness.
